CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: High relative to its narrow scope. It identifies whether options-hedging flows leave a measurable price-level footprint on the most liquid BTC perpetual, which no tested mechanism addresses.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Mean rank of K* among matched placebo strikes is not below the 5th percentile of the uniform-rank null. And the expiry-Friday versus non-expiry-Friday difference in normalized PIN_DIST falls inside the placebo distribution's central 95% band. If both hold, pinning is falsified at this resolution.
CARD.FUNCTION: Test whether Binance BTC perpetual price is attracted toward the maximum-open-interest strike of expiring Deribit options at the 08:00 UTC settlement.
CARD.HORIZON: From the OI snapshot, taken a fixed lead before expiry, to the 08:00 UTC Deribit settlement, with path diagnostics over the final 4 hours.
CARD.MECHANISM: Delta hedging of large net option positions near expiry pulls the underlying toward high-open-interest strikes (pinning). This should show up as a reduced volatility-normalized distance between the Binance perpetual price and the maximum-OI strike at Deribit's 08:00 UTC expiry.
CARD.NAME: Deribit expiry strike-pinning footprint on Binance BTC perpetual price at 08:00 UTC
CARD.OBSERVABLE: PIN_DIST = |ln(P_perp at 08:00 UTC / K*)| divided by trailing 24h realized volatility. K* is the strike with maximum aggregate open interest in the expiring series at a snapshot taken a fixed lead before expiry.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Rank of the normalized PIN_DIST of K* among matched placebo strikes of the same expiring series, pooled across expiries, together with the expiry-versus-non-expiry-Friday difference in median normalized PIN_DIST.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Matched control hours drawn from the same year, weekday, UTC hour and trailing RV bucket, with no mint within 48 hours on either side. Mint timestamps are permuted within year x weekday x hour strata to generate a null distribution of ASYM computed identically.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Two stories predict opposite orderings. In the injection story, new stablecoins arrive, are routed to exchanges and are deployed, so abnormal taker-buy share rises after the mint. In the reactive story, Tether issues against dollar deposits already made by counterparties who have already expressed demand elsewhere, so abnormal flow precedes the mint. Hourly on-chain timestamps against hourly perpetual flow can discriminate between them. Proposed family M, STABLECOIN_SUPPLY_SEQUENCING: temporal ordering between on-chain liquidity creation and venue order flow.

DATA_REQUIRED.DATASET: Ethereum USDT contract Issue and treasury Transfer events (node or public explorer export)
DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Block timestamp, transaction hash and amount for each USDT issuance to the Tether treasury and each treasury outflow

DATA_REQUIRED.DATASET: Tron USDT TRC20 treasury mint and outflow transactions
DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Block timestamp and amount of treasury mints and outflows
Hourly taker-buy quote volume and total quote volume of BTCUSDT perpetual

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It determines the direction of causality between stablecoin supply and venue flow at hourly resolution, a question that is often asserted but rarely tested with point-in-time timestamps.
CARD.FALSIFIER: If both pre-mint and post-mint abnormal taker-buy share fall inside the permutation null's 95% band, mint timing is uninformative about venue flow at hourly resolution and both stories fail. If ASYM is outside the band but shares the pooled sign in fewer than 3 of the 5 years from 2020 to 2024, the sequencing claim is falsified as unstable.
CARD.FUNCTION: Determine whether abnormal Binance BTC perpetual taker-buy share leads or lags on-chain USDT treasury issuance.
CARD.HORIZON: A 24-hour window on each side of the mint block timestamp, at hourly resolution.
CARD.MECHANISM: Stablecoin issuance is either a liquidity injection that precedes crypto demand on venues, or a reactive settlement of demand that has already occurred. The ordering of abnormal taker-buy share around mint block timestamps discriminates between the two.
CARD.NAME: Lead-lag sequencing between USDT treasury issuance and Binance BTC perpetual taker flow
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Mint events are USDT issuance transactions to the Tether treasury on Ethereum and Tron, with block timestamps and amounts. TBS_h is the hourly taker-buy quote volume share of the Binance BTCUSDT perpetual. Abnormal TBS is TBS minus the matched-control mean.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: ASYM: mean abnormal taker-buy share over the 24 hours before the mint minus mean abnormal taker-buy share over the 24 hours after it, pooled across mints above the size threshold.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Placebo levels are offset from round levels by random non-round amounts and matched on approach velocity over the prior 30 minutes, 1-hour RV, UTC hour and weekday. Round-versus-placebo labels are permuted within strata. The null generates both the traversal-time difference and the depth-slope statistic.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Limit-order submitters anchor to round prices, so resting quantity concentrates there. A concentrated queue must be consumed before price can pass, which slows traversal. If slowing exists but is unrelated to measured depth, the channel is behavioral (stop placement, attention) rather than liquidity mechanics. Proposed family N, NOMINAL_LEVEL_LIQUIDITY_TOPOLOGY: how exogenous price-grid focal points shape resting liquidity and path speed.

DATA_REQUIRED.DATASET: Binance USD-M BTCUSDT bookDepth public archive (percentage-band depth)
DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Aggregated resting quantity in percentage bands around mid with snapshot timestamps

DATA_REQUIRED.DATASET: Third-party Binance USD-M BTCUSDT L2 incremental book history
DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Level-resolved resting quantity by price with update timestamps
1m high, low and close for band touch and exit timing

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate to high. It separates a liquidity-mechanics channel from a behavioral one for round-number effects, a distinction that kline-only boundary studies cannot make.
CARD.FALSIFIER: Traversal time at round levels does not differ from placebo levels beyond the permutation band. Or depth concentration is not higher at round levels than at placebo levels. Or a traversal difference exists but has no dependence on DEPTH_CONC; that last outcome falsifies the liquidity channel specifically.
CARD.FUNCTION: Test whether resting depth concentrated at round BTC price levels slows price traversal, and whether any slowing is explained by measured depth.
CARD.HORIZON: From first touch of the band around a level to exit by 0.2% on either side, capped at 6 hours.
CARD.MECHANISM: Resting limit orders cluster at round BTC price levels, forming depth walls that slow price traversal. Deceleration should scale with measured depth concentration at the level.
CARD.NAME: Round-number limit-order clustering and traversal deceleration in the BTC perpetual book
CARD.OBSERVABLE: DEPTH_CONC(L) is resting quantity within ±0.05% of round level L divided by resting quantity in adjacent same-width bands, measured from the snapshot at or before the approach. TRAVERSAL_TIME is the time from first touch of [L-0.1%, L+0.1%] to exit by 0.2% on either side.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Slope of log TRAVERSAL_TIME on DEPTH_CONC across approaches, together with the round-versus-placebo difference in median log TRAVERSAL_TIME.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Three nulls, each computing ZUMBACH_ASYM identically. (1) The time-reversed empirical series, which flips the sign of any true asymmetry. (2) Block-shuffled surrogates preserving one-day blocks. (3) A parametric bootstrap from a fitted symmetric GARCH(1,1), which produces only weak asymmetry.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Participants operating on different horizons respond asymmetrically: coarse-horizon agents' activity feeds fine-horizon volatility, while fine-horizon noise barely affects coarse-horizon decisions. A realized trend also triggers repositioning that raises later volatility. Both effects make the volatility process irreversible in time. Proposed family O, TIME_REVERSAL_ASYMMETRY: statistics that are nonzero only when the arrow of time matters in the volatility cascade.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BTCUSDT perpetual 1m close aggregated to 5m, 15m, 1h and 4h log returns
ETHUSDT perpetual 1m close for replication of the asymmetry statistic

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It establishes whether the cross-scale volatility process is irreversible beyond GARCH. That determines whether multi-horizon volatility models are structurally required for any volatility-conditioned mechanism.
CARD.FALSIFIER: ZUMBACH_ASYM falls inside the central 95% of the symmetric-GARCH bootstrap distribution, or the yearly sign matches the pooled sign in fewer than 3 of the 5 years from 2020 to 2024. The ETH replication is reported but is not needed to falsify.
CARD.FUNCTION: Measure whether the BTC perpetual volatility cascade is irreversible in time, beyond what symmetric GARCH generates.
CARD.HORIZON: Symmetric past and future windows of tau hours around each decision time on a 1h grid; the tau variants are 6, 24 and 72 hours.
CARD.MECHANISM: Coarse-grained past volatility predicts fine-grained future volatility more strongly than fine-grained past volatility predicts coarse-grained future volatility. Past price trends also raise future volatility. Together these make the process irreversible in time (the Zumbach effect and the Lynch-Zumbach cascade).
CARD.NAME: Time-reversal asymmetry (Zumbach effect) in the BTC perpetual volatility cascade
CARD.OBSERVABLE: A(tau) = corr(coarse past RV, fine future RV) - corr(fine past RV, coarse future RV). Coarse RV is the sum of squared coarse-interval returns and fine RV is the sum of squared fine-interval returns over windows of length tau. A secondary trend-volatility asymmetry compares the squared past cumulative return against future RV with the reversed pairing.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: ZUMBACH_ASYM, A(tau) at tau = 24h, estimated monthly and pooled, after removing hour-of-week seasonality.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: A simulated two-venue model with a common efficient price, independent venue noise and partial adjustment at a single constant speed parameter across the whole sample, calibrated to week-specific volatility and noise variance. It generates weekly EPPS_GAP under constant transmission speed. A second, pure-noise null (no lag) generates the Epps curve from noise alone, so that lag can be separated from noise.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Cross-venue price alignment requires intermediaries who observe one venue and act on the other, subject to latency, capital and inventory limits. When their capital is scarce or venue risk rises, alignment slows and correlation at fine sampling intervals drops relative to coarse intervals. The shape of the Epps curve is therefore a clock for cross-venue transmission capacity. Proposed family P, CROSS_VENUE_TRANSMISSION_SPEED: the frequency-scale structure of same-asset co-movement across venues.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: Aligned 5m closes of the Binance BTC perpetual and OKX BTC spot
Quote volume and realized volatility of the BTCUSDT perpetual per week

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It yields a time series of cross-venue transmission speed and tests whether that speed varies beyond noise and volatility, which informs how dislocation-based mechanisms should be normalized.
CARD.FALSIFIER: After controls, the variance and trend of weekly EPPS_GAP lie within the central 95% band of the constant-speed simulation. And the lead-lag cross-correlation at ±5m is explained by the pure-noise null. If both hold, time-varying transmission speed is falsified at this resolution.
CARD.FUNCTION: Characterize the Epps curve of the Binance BTC perpetual versus OKX BTC spot as a time-varying measure of cross-venue transmission speed.
CARD.HORIZON: Weekly estimation windows from Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:55 UTC, with a monthly variant.
CARD.MECHANISM: Correlation between returns of the same asset on two venues rises with the sampling interval (the Epps effect), at a rate set by how quickly intermediaries transmit price information across venues. The gap between fine- and coarse-interval correlation measures transmission speed. It is expected to vary with venue stress and intermediary capital.
CARD.NAME: Cross-venue Epps-curve speed of the Binance BTC perpetual versus OKX spot as a transmission-capacity clock
CARD.OBSERVABLE: For each week, the correlation rho(Delta) between log returns of the Binance perpetual and OKX spot at Delta of 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 minutes. EPPS_GAP = rho(max Delta) - rho(5m). Lead-lag cross-correlation at ±5m is computed as a diagnostic.
CARD.PRIMARY_TARGET: Weekly EPPS_GAP regressed on week index with realized-volatility and quote-volume controls, plus the residual dispersion of EPPS_GAP relative to the constant-speed simulation.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: Within-venue sign-randomization null: jump timing and magnitudes are preserved while signs are flipped at random, which generates DOWN_UP_EXCITATION_RATIO under symmetry. A second null is a symmetric bivariate Hawkes model fitted per venue. For the cross-venue contrast, a block bootstrap by week of the ratio difference in overlapping windows.
CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: In a BTC-margined inverse contract, bullish-side leveraged positions lose on the contract and on the USD value of their collateral at the same time when price falls, so maintenance margin is hit sooner and forced liquidations cascade more readily. Bearish-side positions gain collateral value as price rises, which partly offsets their losses. Linear USDT-margined contracts lack this convexity. Proposed family Q, CONTRACT_DESIGN_REFLEXIVITY: asymmetries in price dynamics induced by margin-currency design.

DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: BitMEX XBTUSD 5m OHLC for jump detection and bipower volatility
BTCUSDT linear perpetual 1m close aggregated to 5m returns

DATA_REQUIRED.DATASET: BitMEX XBTUSD 5m klines via public API
DATA_REQUIRED.OBSERVABLE: XBTUSD 5m OHLC in windows overlapping the Binance linear perpetual
Liquidation side, size and timestamp

CARD.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Moderate. It tests whether contract design is a structural source of downside tail clustering. That bears on whether pre-2020 inverse-contract results can be pooled with linear-contract results.
CARD.FALSIFIER: The pre-2020 XBTUSD DOWN_UP_EXCITATION_RATIO lies within the central 95% of the sign-flip null. Or, in overlapping windows, the XBTUSD ratio minus the Binance linear ratio lies within the block-bootstrap 95% band.
CARD.FUNCTION: Measure whether downside jumps self-excite more strongly than upside jumps in the inverse BitMEX XBTUSD contract, and whether that asymmetry exceeds the one in linear USDT perpetuals.
CARD.HORIZON: The window after each detected jump bar: 30, 60 or 120 minutes.
CARD.MECHANISM: In inverse, coin-margined contracts a price fall also cuts the USD value of the BTC collateral backing bullish-side leveraged positions. Liquidations therefore cascade faster on the way down than on linear contracts, producing stronger self-excitation of downside jumps than of upside jumps.
CARD.NAME: Inverse-contract collateral reflexivity: downside jump clustering in BitMEX XBTUSD versus linear perpetuals
CARD.OBSERVABLE: Signed 5m jumps defined by |r| > k times local bipower volatility. P_down is the probability of another down jump within the window given a down jump, and P_up is the analogue for up jumps. DOWN_UP_EXCITATION_RATIO = P_down / P_up.

CARD.BASELINE_OR_NULL: A pseudo-holiday null. Same-weekday non-holiday dates in the same year and the same seasonal neighborhood are drawn at random and W_INDEX is computed identically. Matching within weekday preserves weekday composition, and the null distribution is built within weekday strata.

CARD.CAUSAL_OR_STRUCTURAL_STORY: Liquidity providers who absorb customer option flow carry an inventory gamma. With positive gamma, delta rebalancing trades against price changes, adding contrarian flow at sub-hour scales. With negative gamma, rebalancing chases price, adding momentum-like flow. If the BTC options market is large enough relative to perpetual depth, this should shift perpetual return autocorrelation. Proposed family T, HEDGING_INVENTORY_FEEDBACK: feedback from derivative-hedging inventory to the underlying's short-horizon dynamics.
